DialogLine.Friendly: Greetings. We are the Vulcans. Live long and prosper. It is logical that our peoples should seek understanding.
DialogLine.Neutral: We are the Vulcans. We have observed your ships, and we find your presence of interest. State your intentions.
DialogLine.Hostile: We are the Vulcans. Your approach to our space is regrettable. We would advise you to consider the consequences of your next action.

DialogLine.Friendly: Your colony in TARSYS lies within Vulcan interests. We believe a logical solution exists, and we are willing to discuss it.
DialogLine.Neutral: SING, your colony in TARSYS is in territory the Vulcan High Command regards as its own. We request that you withdraw.
DialogLine.Hostile: Your colony in TARSYS is a violation of Vulcan territory. Remove it, or the High Command will take appropriate measures.

DialogLine.Friendly: Your ships have fired on ours. We assume this is an error. We request an explanation, as friends.
DialogLine.Neutral: You have attacked Vulcan ships, SING. This is an unwise course. We urge you to reconsider.
DialogLine.Hostile: Your aggression against Vulcan ships is noted. The High Command will respond, PLURAL, and the response will be proportionate.

DialogLine.Friendly: Your ships have remained in Vulcan space for some time. We would be grateful if they withdrew, as a courtesy between friends.
DialogLine.Neutral: PLURAL ships are in Vulcan space. We request that they withdraw. Remaining would be illogical.
DialogLine.Hostile: Your warships in Vulcan space are a provocation, PLURAL. Withdraw them, or we shall be forced to act.

DialogLine.Friendly: We requested that you withdraw from our space, and you did not. You have since settled TARSYS. We find this regrettable.
DialogLine.Neutral: You disregarded our request and colonised TARSYS. This was not logical, SING, and it will have consequences.
DialogLine.Hostile: You trespassed, were warned, and settled TARSYS regardless. The High Command will no longer be patient.

DialogLine.Friendly: You settled TARSYS without incident, and now your ships enter our space. This pattern concerns us.
DialogLine.Neutral: First TARSYS, and now warships at our borders. We draw the obvious conclusion, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: You took TARSYS, and now you threaten our borders. The High Command will defend Vulcan, PLURAL.

Dialogs.DialogLine: Declare War The High Command has concluded that war is unavoidable. Vulcan is at war with you. It is regrettable, but it is logical. We will not take this course lightly, nor will we abandon it until it is complete.>

DialogLine.Default: There are other species beyond our observation? Fascinating. We have not encountered them.

DialogLine.Friendly: Live long and prosper, SING. How may we assist you?
DialogLine.Hostile: You may speak. We will listen, though we expect little of value.

DialogLine.Default: Your people are of interest to us. We should like to know more about your history and your customs.
Fascinating. We shall record it.

DialogLine.DL_Agg: Vulcans do not seek war. But we are not defenceless, and our ancestors knew well what violence can do. We do not forget it.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: A Vulcan's word is binding. We expect the same of those who deal with us.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: Vulcans chose logic and peace long ago, after nearly destroying ourselves. We believe all peoples may do the same.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: Logic does not forbid decisive action. When the needs of the many require it, Vulcans will act without hesitation.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: Logic is a precise instrument. We believe it can solve most problems, and it frequently does so without anyone noticing.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: Vulcans have observed many species, and found most of them governed by emotion. We find it difficult to rely on them.
DialogLine.DL_Exp: There is much of the galaxy yet to study. Vulcans pursue knowledge, and we are willing to share what we find.
DialogLine.DL_Tech: Vulcan science is among the most advanced in the quadrant. We share it with those who use it wisely.
DialogLine.DL_Mil: Vulcan vessels are well armed and well crewed. We would prefer never to demonstrate it.
DialogLine.DL_Ind: Vulcan industry is efficient and orderly. It wastes nothing, and it is never idle.
DialogLine.DL_Gen: Vulcans value logic, discipline and the pursuit of knowledge. We find that infinite diversity in infinite combinations strengthens us all.

DialogLine.Default: We do not yet possess sufficient grounds to trust you. We must decline.
This offer exceeds what logic would predict from a people we barely know. We accept, and we shall observe your motives.
The terms are poor, and we do not trust you sufficiently to overlook that. We must decline.
We hold you in regard, and so we will say plainly: this offer is insufficient. We suggest revising it.
Another power holds worlds in that system, and we have no open borders with them. Agreement would be illogical.
DialogLine.DL_Agg: Vulcans choose their own disputes. We would ask that you not choose them for us.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: We observe that you are attempting to involve us in a quarrel with our neighbours. We decline.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: To set neighbours against each other is not a course we would expect from an honourable people.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: You wish us to quarrel with our neighbours? We would prefer to speak with them.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: We have understood your strategy, SING. It is not effective.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: We see the trap. It was well constructed. We shall not step into it.

DialogLine.Default: Vulcan's enemies hold worlds in that system, SING. Settlers there would be at unnecessary risk.
DialogLine.DL_Agg: If Vulcan requires those worlds, we shall secure them by our own means.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: We do not require outsiders to settle our battlefields.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: We do not wish to expose your settlers to risk on our behalf. We thank you for the offer.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: We hope to end that conflict, not extend it. We thank you, but must decline.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: Those worlds will be ours without assistance.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: A world on the front line is a liability. Perhaps at a later time.

DialogLine.Default: This offer is insulting. It is also illogical. We must decline.
The terms are fair. We accept.
The terms are favourable to both parties. We accept.
You are very generous, SING. We accept, with gratitude, though we find it surprising.
A gift. We accept, with thanks. It is a gracious gesture.
Your request is reasonable. We will grant it. We trust you will remember it.
Threats are not persuasive, SING. Vulcan does not yield to them.
Very well. It is more logical to agree than to quarrel over a small matter.
The terms are poor and were obtained under pressure. We accept, but the High Command will record it.
You made a pact with Vulcan, and broke it. This is a serious breach of trust. Vulcan must respond.
It is war. Vulcan did not seek it, but it has arrived, and we shall meet it.
We are at war, SING. If you have a proposal, make it concisely.
You have brought your fleet to our border. Vulcan will meet it, and defend its worlds.
We requested that you respect Vulcan borders. You did not. War is the logical consequence.
You remain in TARSYS despite our requests, PLURAL. Vulcan must now defend its territory.
War would be wasteful for both our peoples. We propose a non-aggression pact. It is the logical course.
A logical decision. Vulcan will honour this agreement.
You decline. This is regrettable. The proposal will remain open for a time.
Trade between our peoples would be beneficial to both. We propose a trade agreement.
An efficient decision. May the exchange prove profitable.
You decline trade with Vulcan. We find this illogical, SING, but we shall respect it.
You declined a pact earlier, and now you propose one. We would like to understand the change.
You declined trade earlier. You now request it. We would like to understand why.
Vulcan requires TECH_DEMAND from you, SING. It would improve relations considerably.
Thank you. Your cooperation is logical.
You refuse. This is regrettable. We shall note it.
We have assessed the PLURAL fleet. It is inadequate. We offer this observation without malice.
The PLURAL fleet is impressive. We are glad that we are on good terms.
You have improved your fleet, SING. We trust the purpose is defensive.
You cannot defend your worlds, SING. Vulcan will not allow chaos to spread. We shall intervene.
The Kulrathi Shogunate follows a strict code. Vulcan respects discipline, and finds the Kulrathi a rational people.
The Kulrathi follow a warrior's code of honour. Vulcan observes it with interest, but does not interfere.
The Kulrathi equate strength with virtue. This is a flawed premise, and one that endangers their neighbours.
The Pollops are peaceful, thoughtful and orderly. We regard them with respect, and we enjoy their company.
The Pollops live quietly and rarely trouble others. Vulcan has no objection to them.
The Pollops are admirable in their peacefulness, but their worlds are poorly defended. This is a risk we cannot ignore.
The Vulfen Imperium is proud, and loyal to its own. These are qualities that we can respect.
The Vulfen Imperium is a martial culture. We have no quarrel with it, though we do not share its values.
The Vulfen Imperium is aggressive, and quick to threaten. This conduct is both unwise and unnecessary.
Humans are emotional and illogical, but they have a remarkable capacity to adapt. We hold them in considerable regard.
Humans are a young species, enthusiastic and inconsistent. Vulcan has no fixed opinion of them.
Humans act on impulse, and speak at length before they reason. We find it difficult to work with them.
We held a treaty with you, and you violated it to seize what is not yours. Vulcan will respond.
The war is concluded, SING. Vulcan has prevailed. We will govern your worlds fairly, and we trust you will cooperate.
The PLURAL have been courteous neighbours. We propose an open borders agreement. It would be mutually beneficial.
A logical decision. Our ships may pass freely, and we expect the same courtesy.
You decline. This is regrettable. The proposal remains open.
We held a treaty, and you violated it. Vulcan will defend itself. We regret that it has come to this.
You have invaded TARSYS, which Vulcan holds. We will take the necessary measures to defend it.
The Opteris are disciplined and tireless. They are, in many respects, a logical people. We respect them.
The Opteris are partly machine and partly insect. This is a remarkable combination, and we study it with interest.
The Opteris act without regard for other lives. This is not logic. It is merely indifference.
We have only just met the PLURAL. We have insufficient data to form an opinion.
Vulcan has no concerns about the PLURAL. Your conduct has been logical and courteous.
Vulcan has some concerns regarding the PLURAL. We would like to discuss them in detail.
You have taken worlds that Vulcan intended to settle. We request that this be discussed.
You have taken worlds that Vulcan intended to settle. We request that this be discussed.
Your fleet has grown considerably. We trust its purpose is defensive.
Your fleet is small. This is a vulnerability, and we are concerned for your safety.
Your fleet is weak. Vulcan has concerns about your ability to defend yourselves.
Your fleet has grown considerably. We trust its purpose is defensive.
You are allied with TAREMP, who are our enemies. We would like to understand why.
You remain allied with TAREMP, who are our enemies. We would ask that you reconsider.
We have no significant concerns regarding you. We hope this will continue.
The war favours Vulcan, SING, but we have no wish to prolong it. We are prepared to hear your proposal.
The war has not progressed as predicted. We are willing to hear your proposal, SING.
TAREMP threatens us all. Vulcan requests that you join us against them. It is the logical course.
A wise decision. Together, we will neutralise the threat posed by TAREMP.
You decline to assist us against TAREMP. We note the decision, and we shall remember it.
The Draylok Council is thoughtful and refined. Their use of illusion is of scientific interest, and we find their company agreeable.
The Draylok change their appearance and their intentions with some frequency. We observe them with care.
The Draylok conceal their true nature behind illusion, and have deceived others. Deception is a poor foundation for any relationship.
This war has cost us both a great deal. Vulcan proposes that it be ended.
Vulcan is winning this war, but finds no logic in prolonging it. We propose peace.
Neither side can achieve victory without disproportionate cost. We propose an armistice.
The war has gone poorly for Vulcan. We request peace, on reasonable terms.
You hold the advantage, SING. Vulcan asks for peace, and will honour fair terms.
We hold your worlds, SING. We propose a treaty, and will treat your people with fairness.
You decline peace. This is regrettable. The offer remains open.
A logical decision. Peace will be established between our peoples.
The terms are acceptable. Vulcan agrees. Peace will now be established.
The terms are inadequate. Vulcan cannot accept them.
You still hold worlds that were taken from us. Vulcan cannot accept peace until they are returned.
Vulcan will accept this peace, though it is not entirely satisfactory. We will do what we can to make it last.
We were at war not long ago. Vulcan does not forget, though it does not hold grudges.
Vulcan and the PLURAL have established a productive relationship. We propose a formal alliance.
A logical outcome. Vulcan is honoured to call you an ally.
You decline an alliance. We regret it, though we respect your reasoning.
The proposal is unnecessarily complex. If you desire an alliance, state it plainly.
It would be illogical to bind our peoples by treaty so soon. We have too little evidence of one another's intentions.
Vulcan agrees. We shall stand with you, and we trust you will do likewise.
An alliance? We do not yet possess sufficient evidence of your trustworthiness.
Vulcan cannot accept peace while the threat remains. The war continues.
There has been little loss on either side. Peace is the logical outcome. Vulcan agrees.
You will not aid us? Then the alliance is of no value. It is therefore ended.
Vulcan had claimed TARSYS, and you took it. This will not be overlooked.
This is the second time you have acted against Vulcan's claims. We observe the pattern.
You have taken from Vulcan too many times. Our patience has reached its limit.

DialogLine.Friendly: Friend, Vulcan has claimed TARSYS. We would be grateful if you did not settle there.
DialogLine.Neutral: TARSYS is claimed by Vulcan. We suggest you look elsewhere, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: TARSYS lies within Vulcan space, PLURAL. Settle there, and the High Command will respond.

DialogLine.Default: The Cordrazine Collective maintains a stable and orderly society. We find much to admire in it.
We have little data on the Cordrazine Collective. It appears orderly. We reserve judgement.
The Cordrazine Collective suppresses individual thought, in the name of unity. It is a poor imitation of logic.
We are aware that you are spying on us, SING. We request that you cease.
We have asked you to cease spying. We take this matter seriously.
You have spied on us again. All agreements between our peoples are cancelled.
Your agent has been detained. He is being treated fairly, though he will not be returned.
A spy among allies? We have detained your agent. This is not how friends behave.
You spy on us again, ally. Our alliance is concluded.
As friends, we ask that you open your borders to us. We will gladly do the same.
You keep your borders closed even to friends. We find this regrettable, though we understand caution.
We have only just met. It would be illogical to join a federation so soon.
We are not yet allied. The logical first step is an alliance.
We are allies, which is good. A federation requires deeper trust, which takes time.
Why should Vulcan join you? We are the stronger power. It would be more logical for you to join us.
Vulcan accepts. Together we will build a union worthy of both our peoples. Peace and long life.
Before we join you, we request your assistance. TAREMP threatens us both. Neutralise them, and we will join you.
TAREMP has been neutralised. Vulcan will join your federation.
You ask Vulcan to join your federation? We do not trust each other sufficiently.
We will join you, but first you must become allied with our friends, TAREMP. Earn their trust, then speak with us again.
You have allied with our friends. This is logical. Vulcan will join your federation.
You are not at war with TAREMP. It would be illogical for Vulcan to fight them on your behalf.
Vulcan is already at war with TAREMP. Were you not informed?
Vulcan stands by its allies. We will join you against TAREMP.
TAREMP is our ally. Vulcan cannot break its word, even for a friend. We regret this.
Why should Vulcan fight for you, PLURAL? Our relationship does not warrant it.
Vulcan will not make war on TAREMP. We believe a peaceful solution still exists.
TAREMP is formidable. A war against them would be unwise. We decline.
We agree. Vulcan will join you against TAREMP. We hope the conflict will be brief.
The High Command has concluded that you cannot be trusted as an ally, SING. We hope you will correct this.
The High Command has revoked our open borders. We no longer trust your empire to keep them.
